title: Wonders of the World
goals: Compare three or more things with superlatives: the tallest, the most interesting, the least expensive, the best.
Talk about places with the most + noun and one of the + superlative + plural noun.
Ask about and give measurements with How high / long / wide / deep…? and with units (meters, kilometers, degrees).
Name natural wonders and structures: glacier, reef, suspension bridge, skyscraper.
Show that you are listening with interest, using really / sure (It really is. It sure does.).
Write sentences with extra information between commas (Mount Fuji, a volcano in Japan, is famous).

learn.title: Superlatives: the -est / the most / the least
learn.html:
The superlative compares three or more things and points out the one at the extreme. In English, you use the + superlative adjective.

Type of adjectiveRuleExample
Short (1 syllable)the + adj + -esttall → the tallest
Ends in -e+ -stlarge → the largest
Ends in vowel + consonantdouble the consonant + -estbig → the biggest, hot → the hottest
2 syllables ending in -yy → i + -estbusy → the busiest
Long (2+ syllables)the most / least + adjthe most interesting, the least expensive
Irregular—good → the best, bad → the worst

To say “the least…”, use the least: the least crowded beach. After the superlative, use in with places or groups (in the world, in my family) and of with periods or sets (of the year, of all).

watch.wrong: It's the most tall building in the city.
watch.right: It's the tallest building in the city.
watch.why: Short adjectives take -est, not the most.

watch.wrong: This is the most good restaurant in town.
watch.right: This is the best restaurant in town.

watch.wrong: It's the biggest city of the country.
watch.right: It's the biggest city in the country.
watch.why: With places, use in, not of.

watch.wrong: She is the more intelligent student.
watch.right: She is the most intelligent student.
watch.why: The superlative uses the most, not more.

learn.title: the most + noun and one of the + superlative
learn.html:
With nouns, the most means “more than any other”: Which country has the most tourism? Which stadium has the most seats? For the opposite, use the fewest (countable nouns) or the least (uncountable nouns).

To say “one of the most…”, use one of the + superlative + plural noun:

  • Mexico City is one of the biggest cities in the world.
  • It's one of the most beautiful beaches I've ever seen.

For personal experience, use the present perfect: It's the best trip I've ever taken. (= of all the trips in my life so far).

watch.wrong: It's one of the tallest building in the world.
watch.right: It's one of the tallest buildings in the world.
watch.why: After one of the, use a plural noun.

watch.wrong: Which city has the most big airport?
watch.right: Which city has the biggest airport?
watch.why: If the noun is not a measurement, the short adjective takes -est.

watch.wrong: It's the best trip I went.
watch.right: It's the best trip I've ever taken.
watch.why: For your whole life up to now, use the present perfect (I've ever + past participle).

learn.title: How + adjective: measurements and facts
learn.html:
To ask about measurements, use How + adjective + be + subject? With high, long, wide, deep, tall, the answer repeats the adjective after the measurement:

QuestionAnswer
How high is Mount Everest?It's 8,850 meters (29,035 feet) high.
How long is the Nile River?It's 6,695 kilometers (4,160 miles) long.
How wide is the Grand Canyon?It's about 29 kilometers (18 miles) wide.
How deep is the Pacific Ocean?It's about 11,000 meters deep.
How tall is the tower?It's 300 meters tall.

With large and hot, you do NOT repeat the adjective: How large is the Sahara? — It's 9.1 million square kilometers. / How hot does it get in Death Valley? — It can reach 48 degrees Celsius.

Units and numbers: 1 km = 0.62 miles; 1 m = 3.28 feet; 0°C = 32°F. You say six thousand five hundred (and) twenty-nine (6,529), a million (1,000,000) and seven point seven (7.7). In English, a comma separates the thousands: 6,529.

watch.why: The adjective goes right after How.
In English, use be + measurement + adjective, not “it has … of height”.

watch.wrong: How much long is the river?
watch.why: Much is not used between How and the adjective.
With large, you don't repeat the adjective.

learn.title: Strategy: being a supportive listener (really / sure)
learn.html:
To show you agree with someone, reply with a short phrase: pronoun + really / sure + auxiliary. The auxiliary repeats the tense of what the other person said.

Says A…You reply B…
Verb be: This is the most incredible place!Yeah, it really is.
Simple present: It feels good to be out of the city.It sure does.
Present perfect: Well, it's been a great day.It really has.
Modal: We should go hiking there sometime.We really should.

You can also use the superlative for emphasis in your opinions: This is the most incredible place! I had the best time.

learn.title: Writing: adding information with commas
learn.html:
You can join two sentences into one if the second one only gives extra information about something. The extra information is written between commas.

  • Mount Aconcagua is the highest mountain in Argentina. + It is a peak in the Andes. → Mount Aconcagua, a peak in the Andes, is the highest mountain in Argentina. (commas before and after, because it's in the middle)
  • Many people visit the Andes. + They are the longest mountain range in the world. → Many people visit the Andes, the longest mountain range in the world. (one comma before it, because it comes at the end)

This extra information is a noun phrase: it usually starts with a, an or the. It has no verb of its own.

watch.wrong: Cancún a city on the coast is very popular.
watch.right: Cancún, a city on the coast, is very popular.
watch.why: Extra information in the middle goes between two commas.

watch.wrong: Tulum, is an ancient city, is near the sea.
watch.right: Tulum, an ancient city, is near the sea.
watch.why: Extra information has no verb of its own (is).

watch.wrong: We visited Lake Chapala. The largest lake in Mexico.
watch.right: We visited Lake Chapala, the largest lake in Mexico.
watch.why: A loose fragment is not a sentence on its own: join it with a comma.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• This is the most incredible place! — emphasizing an opinion with a superlative.
  • I had the best time. — saying you had a great time.
  • Yeah, it really is. / It sure does. / It really has. / We really should. — showing agreement.
  • How long / high / wide / deep is …? — asking about measurements.
  • It's about … meters/kilometers long. — giving an approximate measurement.
  • It's one of the most … in the world. — saying something is among the best.
  • Did you know that …? — sharing an interesting fact.

write.prompt: Write an email to a friend (120 to 180 words) about the most impressive place you know: where it is, what it's like, and what you did there. Include at least three superlatives and two measurements (for example, how high or how long). Opening example: Last year I visited the most incredible place I've ever seen…
checklist: One measurement (It's … meters high / kilometers long)
in the world / in the city (not of)
One expression with best or most for emphasis (I had the best time)
write.model:
Hi Carlos,

Last year I visited the most incredible place I've ever seen: Copper Canyon in Chihuahua. It is one of the biggest canyons in the world, and in some places it is about 1,800 meters deep. The train ride through the mountains is the most beautiful trip in Mexico, and it is about 650 kilometers long.

We stayed in a small town called Creel, which is the cheapest place to sleep near the canyon. On the first day, we hiked to a lake, and the water was the coldest I've ever touched! On the second day, we took a cable car and saw the most amazing views of the canyon. It was the least crowded place I visited on my trip, so it was very quiet.

I had the best time of my life there, and the food was delicious, too. The people in the town are some of the friendliest in the country. You must come with me next year! Write to me soon and tell me when you are free.

Your friend,
Luis

write.prompt: Write an information card (120 to 180 words) about three wonders of Mexico or of your region. For each one, use extra information between commas and at least one measurement. Opening example: Popocatépetl, an active volcano near Mexico City, is…
checklist: Extra information with commas before and after
One measurement per place, with the correct adjective
Use of the / a / an in the extra information
write.model:
Three Wonders of Mexico

Popocatepetl, an active volcano near Mexico City, is one of the most famous mountains in the country. It is about 5,400 meters high, and on a clear day you can see it from the capital. It is the second highest peak in Mexico.

Chichen Itza, a Maya city in Yucatan, is a very popular place for tourists. Its main pyramid, El Castillo, is about 30 meters high. It is one of the most important ruins in the world, and it receives more than a million visitors every year.

Sumidero Canyon, a deep gorge in Chiapas, is a beautiful place to visit by boat. The cliffs, which are covered in green plants, are about 1,000 meters high. The river that runs through the canyon, the Grijalva, is a great place to see crocodiles and birds. The boat trip is about 35 kilometers long and takes two hours.

All three places are among the best reasons to visit Mexico.

reading.title: Riding the train through the Copper Canyon
reading.intro: Read Marina's travel blog and answer the questions.
paragraphs: Last month my brother Daniel and I took the most exciting trip of our lives: a train ride through the Copper Canyon in northern Mexico. Many people say it is the most beautiful place in the country, and now I agree. The canyon system is bigger than the Grand Canyon in the United States, and some parts are almost two kilometers deep.

The train is called the Chepe. It is about 650 kilometers long, and it crosses many bridges and goes through dozens of tunnels. When the train goes over the highest bridge, it moves very slowly, so you can take photos. Daniel, who is afraid of heights, closed his eyes the whole time. I laughed, but honestly I was a little scared too.

The weather changes a lot in the canyon. At the top, it was only 2 degrees Celsius (about 36 degrees Fahrenheit) in the morning, and we needed our warmest jackets. At the bottom, it can reach 40 degrees Celsius in summer. The guide told us that the canyon has the most different kinds of plants and animals in the region, from pine forests to tropical areas.

On the second day we met a Rarámuri family, people who are famous for being some of the best long-distance runners in the world. They sell handmade baskets, the most popular souvenir in the area, and they showed us how they make them. The woman asked my brother to try, and he made the worst basket in history. We all laughed.

I had the best time of my life on this trip. The only problem was the food on the train, which was the most expensive I have ever eaten, and it was not very good. But the views, the people and the quiet were incredible. Next year, we want to go back and go hiking at the bottom of the canyon. If you ask me, everyone should see this place at least once.

glossary.def: feeling fear when you are high up, like on a cliff or a tall building
a long passage dug under the ground or through a mountain
a person who shows visitors around a place and explains it
made by hand, not by a machine
a container made of woven material such as straw or wicker
an object you buy to remember a place you visited
what you can see from a place, especially beautiful landscapes
not less than a certain amount; the smallest amount
